title: Operational safety contracts, cache-priming service, and rollout leash added to Serving PRD
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: This ticket captures PRD-level requirement changes derived from a recent incident where aggressive autoscale and synchronous KV cache eviction caused a cascade of cold-start latency and increased tail error rates for hosted customers. The postmortem recommended operational runbooks, a cache-priming path, stricter rollout gating, and measurable acceptance tests. This PRD update introduces three primary deliverables: 1) Operational Safety Contracts (boolean/guard rails surfaced in the console and API for canaries), 2) a lightweight Cache Priming Service to shepherd traffic during regenerations, and 3) a Rollout Leash that constrains concurrency and automatically enacts an immediate, verifiable rollback when defined SLO regressions are detected.
scope_changes: Add new product features (console flags and API toggles), a small stateful priming service deployed alongside runtime nodes, instrumented observability hooks (trace IDs and synthetic checks), and new acceptance tests in staging. No changes to model formats or public inference API payload shapes. Adds 1 FTE QA and 0.5 FTE DevOps for initial rollout support.
acceptance_criteria: Safety contracts UI: Console exposes a toggle per-deployment 'Operational Safety' with options {Off, Canary-only, Enforced} and an API equivalent; toggles persist in deployment config and are returned by GET /deployments/{id}
Cache Priming Service: New service can accept a prefix list and pre-populate KV caches within 2x of normal warm-serving latency for 99th percentile under test harness conditions

Rollout Leash: During canary rollout, concurrency must be limited to <= 10% of target pool unless 'Operational Safety' set to Off; if tail-latency (p95) increases >20% or error-rate increases >1% for >3 minutes, automated rollback is triggered

Runbook Verification: On-call can execute runbook steps in staging and produce a pdf runbook execution record; runbook steps must include cache-priming trigger, synthetic traffic sweep, and canary rollback simulation
Synthetic Checks: Synthetic job verifies cold-start tail latency is within target (p99 < 1.8x baseline) after cache regen following priming; results must be visible in Console dashboard
Observability: Every priming and rollout action emits a correlated trace_id and an event to the audit log; traces link to a dashboard widget showing primed keys and success/failure counts

Load Test: Canary rollback triggers verified in automated canary harness under 150% expected canary traffic with failure injection; rollback completes within 5 minutes and reduces error-rate to pre-rollout baseline
decisions: Favor operational controls over automatic model substitution for this class of incident — product-level safety contracts are preferred to reduce surprising behavior for customers
Cache Priming Service will be a small stateful sidecar deployed in the serving pool rather than baked into the core runtime to reduce risk and allow iterative improvements
Rollout leash thresholds will be configurable per-customer but default to conservative values defined in this PRD
Do not change the public inference API surface in this rollout; all new controls are configuration and console/API-first
tradeoffs: Adds operational complexity and a small steady-state cost for priming traffic. The sidecar approach speeds iteration but increases deployment topology complexity. Conservative default limits may slow rollouts for large customers; we will expose per-customer overrides with a documented approval flow. We accepted additional observability events (cost) to achieve verifiable rollback conditions.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (staging): Implement priming service and safety toggle; run internal synthetic sweep for 2 weeks
Phase 1 (controlled): Enable 'Canary-only' safety contracts for internal customers and 3 trusted beta customers; collect metrics for 4 weeks
Phase 2 (gradual): Default safety contract to 'Canary-only' for new deployments; allow existing customers to opt-in
Phase 3 (enforced): After metrics validation and exec sign-off, flip default to 'Enforced' for sensitive tiers and add to Dedicated offering release notes
test_plan: Unit tests for toggles and API surface
End-to-end staging tests: simulate cache eviction and measure priming effectiveness
Synthetic regression jobs added to nightly that verify p95/p99 behavior for cold-start scenarios
Canary automation: inject errors and verify automated rollback within SLA
Security/pen test scoped to console toggles and audit log exposure
